definition: A JavaScript library for describing and updating user interfaces through components. React manages when components render and applies the necessary changes to the displayed interface.
The visible controls and information through which a person uses software, such as buttons, lists and form fields.
A reusable part of a React user interface. A function component is a JavaScript function that describes its output using values such as JSX.
One particular occurrence of a component in the rendered UI. Separate instances can use the same function definition while keeping independent state.
A JavaScript syntax extension for writing HTML-like element descriptions. A build tool transforms JSX into JavaScript; it is not ordinary HTML or directly executable browser-script syntax.
The programming language used for the component functions and calculations in this course. JSX is an additional syntax transformed into JavaScript before execution.
HyperText Markup Language: the tag-based language that gives web documents their structure. JSX looks similar but follows its own stricter syntax rules.
Cascading Style Sheets: the language used to describe a web document’s appearance and layout. React elements can select CSS classes using className.
Document Object Model: the browser’s tree of objects representing a page. React commits necessary changes to this tree after calculating its UI description.
A description of a piece of UI, including its element type and props. JSX produces element descriptions; they are not themselves live browser DOM nodes.
Building a larger UI by combining smaller components. A wrapper can accept nested content through children instead of deciding every possible content layout itself.
The component at the starting point of a React component tree. A prepared app mounts this component into the page, and it can return further components.
The build step that converts JSX syntax into JavaScript calls describing elements. The modern transform supplies JSX runtime calls without requiring a React import solely for JSX syntax.
JavaScript code that produces a value, such as a variable reference or function call. JSX braces accept expressions; statements such as if cannot go directly inside them.
An instruction forming part of a JavaScript program, such as a declaration, return or if statement. A statement is not generally interchangeable with an expression that supplies a JSX value.
Text written directly as a string value, such as "Ada". In JSX attributes, quoted text supplies a literal string rather than reading a variable with the same spelling.
JavaScript syntax that reads selected values from an object or array into local bindings. Object patterns select property names; array patterns select positions.
A compact JavaScript function expression written using =>. An expression body returns its value implicitly; a block body needs an explicit return to return a value.
A function passed to another operation so that operation can call it. Array map calls its callback for each item, while an event callback runs when its event is handled.
A JavaScript array method that returns a new array containing the result of calling a callback for each present item. In React it is commonly used to turn records into JSX elements.
A JavaScript array method that returns a new array containing the items for which its callback returns a truthy value. It selects items rather than transforming each retained item.

A JavaScript file executed under the language's module rules, with import and export available for sharing values. This programming meaning is separate from a module grouping lessons in the study app.
A JavaScript declaration making a value available to another module. A default export supplies the file’s default value; a named export is selected by its exported name.
A JavaScript declaration that obtains exported values from another module. Default imports use no braces; named imports select export names with braces.
A file location interpreted relative to the importing file, such as ./Badge.jsx for a neighbouring module. It is different from a package name such as react.
A React grouping that can contain several children without adding a wrapper DOM element. The short JSX syntax is an opening <> and closing </>.
Elements that share the same immediate parent in a tree. React list keys distinguish items among siblings rather than across the entire application.
The React DOM prop specifying an element’s CSS class names. Those names select styling rules; they do not define a custom React component.
A naming style that joins words and capitalises the first letter of later words, as in backgroundColor. Most React DOM prop names and inline style property names use it.
Styling supplied directly to a React DOM element through its style prop. Its value is a JavaScript object whose property names are generally camelCase, rather than an HTML style string.
Accessible Rich Internet Applications: attributes that provide accessibility semantics. React DOM uses the standard hyphenated spelling for attributes such as aria-label.
Inputs a parent supplies to a React component. A child reads its props without mutating them; a later render can provide different values.
A component whose returned UI contains a particular child component. Data can flow from that parent to the child through props.
A component used inside another component’s returned UI. Its props are supplied by that parent; nested JSX content is accessible through the separate children prop.
The React prop containing content nested between a component’s opening and closing JSX tags. A wrapper can render it to accept caller-chosen content.
The rule that a component must not change the props or passed values it receives. It does not mean every JavaScript object passed as a prop is deeply frozen.
A JavaScript fallback used when a supplied argument or destructured property is undefined. It does not replace explicit values such as null or an empty string.
Choosing different React output according to inputs, using normal JavaScript conditions. Returning null contributes no visible content from that component.
The JavaScript conditional expression written as a condition, ?, one value, :, and another value. It produces one of those values and can be used inside JSX braces.
The JavaScript operator &&, which returns its left operand when that is falsy and otherwise returns its right operand. A numeric zero on the left remains zero, which React can display.
A JavaScript value treated as true when used as a condition. It need not be the boolean true; for example, a non-empty string is truthy.
A JavaScript value treated as false in a condition, such as false, zero, an empty string, null or undefined. Falsy does not mean that React hides the value: numeric zero is still renderable text.
A true or false JavaScript value. Boolean children produce no visible text in React, unlike numeric children such as zero.
A JavaScript value used here to explicitly represent no content. A component can return null to contribute no visible UI.
A JavaScript value commonly produced by a missing property or a function without a returned value. React does not display undefined children, and destructuring defaults apply to undefined inputs.
A special React value identifying an element among siblings so React can match it across list updates. It should stay stable for the same item and is not passed to the child as an ordinary prop.
The numeric position of an item in a JavaScript array, starting at zero. A position can change when records are inserted or reordered, so it is often unsuitable as an editable list item’s identity.
React calling components to calculate their UI descriptions. Rendering can repeat and does not itself mean that a DOM change has been committed.
The stage in which React applies the necessary changes to the browser’s DOM after rendering. It is separate from the browser painting the visible screen.
A render calculation that produces the same result for the same props, state and context without changing pre-existing values. Building fresh local arrays can still be pure.
Observable work beyond calculating a function’s returned value, such as modifying shared data or sending a request. Render should avoid it because React may repeat the calculation.
Changing an existing object or array. Mutating received props during render is forbidden; changing a fresh object created only for the current calculation can be safe.
A function called in response to an interaction such as activating a button. Pass the function to onClick instead of calling it while rendering.
The React DOM prop that supplies a click event handler to an element. Its value should be a function for React to call when the click is handled.
Data React remembers for a particular component instance between renders. A state setter requests an update; state is not permanent storage across page reloads or every removal.
A React Hook returning the current state value and a setter function for a component instance. Its initial value starts that instance’s state rather than resetting it on each render.
The function returned by useState to request a state update. It supplies the new value for a later render instead of changing the current render’s state variable in place.

A React function that makes a React feature available to a function component or custom Hook. Ordinary Hooks such as useState must be called at the top level, not inside conditions, loops or handlers.
A function passed to a state setter that receives the pending previous state and returns the next state. React processes it when applying the queued update.
A variable belonging to one function call, such as an array created inside a render. Unlike React state, an ordinary component local is not remembered by React for the next call.
The React library that renders component output into the browser DOM. React calculates the UI and React DOM applies the required changes to page elements.
A named input in a JavaScript function definition. A component parameter can use object destructuring to read selected props.
How information moves through React components. Parents pass props down; a child can call a supplied callback to request that an owner update data.
The starting value supplied for a component instance’s state. React uses it to initialise useState; it does not reset existing state on each render.
A JavaScript string containing no characters, written as two adjacent quote marks. It is falsy in a condition but is not undefined, so a destructuring default does not replace it.

Provided by a language, browser or library rather than written by the application's author. The browser provides elements such as headings and buttons, while React provides built-in Hooks such as useState.
A JavaScript array method that returns one string made from its items separated by a chosen string. It does not change the original array.
example: Joining Ada and Grace with a comma and space produces Ada, Grace.

definition: A JavaScript string method that returns an upper-case version of the string. It returns a new string rather than changing the original value.
The CSS length unit written px and used for dimensions such as padding. A CSS pixel does not necessarily correspond to one physical screen pixel.
example: padding: '8px' requests eight CSS pixels of padding.

definition: A JavaScript error raised, for example, when code tries to read a variable that has not been declared in an available scope. This is different from reading a declared variable whose value is undefined.
